paraphrase: Khedrup Je refutes the view that the ultimate is truly established, permanent and empty only of other: whatever is truly established would be an object for grasping at true existence, and such a view falls to the extreme of permanence, indistinguishable from the self asserted by non-Buddhists.
speaker: Khedrup Je
notes: Recalled as a theme of the Great Digest (stong thun chen mo); exact place and wording not recalled.
translation_basis: Tibetan (paraphrase by the unit from memory; no text consulted)

paraphrase: Khedrup Je argues that the object of negation must be precisely identified and that Madhyamaka reasoning negates inherent existence, not conventional existence; he criticises other Tibetan readings of the view.
